title: Public guide
description: An index of the public articles and language downloads, with notes on what the accounts can establish.

title: Spiritual practice, communion and beliefs about the dead
description: Spiritual practitioners seek contact through dreams, rituals and familiar objects. Even a convincing encounter can be difficult to interpret.

title: Dverghamar: public atlas guide
description: Eight geographic notes on the sunward lands, twilight settlements and dark country of Dverghamar.

title: Dverghamar: landscapes and settlement life
description: Mountain homes depend on surface farms, waterways and machinery. Local rock, rain and shelter determine where settlements can thrive.

title: Dverghamar
description: The dwarven world has permanent day and night. Most settlements occupy watered valleys and mountain districts between them.

title: Elven peoples and traditions
description: Four Elven traditions, their practical arts and childhood customs, and their relationship with Dorrenath and other Wayroots.

title: Enchantments, heirlooms and artifacts
description: How enchanters prepare objects for later use, how enchantments wear out, and how an ordinary possession can become an artifact.

title: Erde: public atlas guide
description: Five geographic notes on Erde’s lands, mountain passages, ancestral migrations and regional contact.

title: Erde: detailed regional history and magical institutions
description: River defenses delay migration; refuge networks help communities survive disaster. A detailed history of four regions and their magical institutions.

title: Erde: peoples and regional histories
description: The early peoples of Erde, their encounters with later settlers, and the regional traditions that preserve their communities.

title: Erde
description: Humans, hobbit lineages and Goblin peoples inhabit Erde’s continents and islands. Their histories follow rivers, mountain corridors and coastal routes.

title: Dwarven natural history
description: Naturalists compare the Hamarkorar with other native animals to investigate their six-limbed ancestry and adaptations to different habitats.

title: Familiars and shapeshifting in practice
description: A familiar keeps its own mind while sharing a magical bond. Training may lead to shapeshifting, with lasting costs when a bond is lost.

title: Gnomes: a comparative account of body, house, kinship and craft
description: A Gnome natural history of bodies and living houses, from birth and household founding to medicine, machinery and houses that become persons.

title: Gnomes
description: Gnomes have bodies of branching fibers and cultivate living homes. Their houses, governments and ancestral customs vary widely.

title: Goblins: a comparative natural history
description: A human naturalist compares Goblin bodies, habitats and families, and investigates their strange passages and the green Alchemical lineage.

title: The Hamarkorar
description: Dverghamar’s native dwarven peoples have four arms and two legs. They build homes within rock and share several traditions of household care.

title: Jotun societies and their reputations
description: Mountain societies differ in their treatment of guests, neighbors and captives. Accounts of violent clans sometimes grow in the retelling.

title: The Jotun
description: Dverghamar’s cold-adapted mountain people; their detailed anatomy remains unsettled.

title: Korvar and the language family
description: Korvar is the common language taught across the dwarven regions. Start with its basic roots, then turn to pronunciation, grammar and examples.

title: Korvar in use
description: 97 Korvar sentences with translations and grammar notes, from introductions and household requests to connected passages.

title: Five regional languages
description: Compare Kamvar, Hamarvar, Dravvar, Nattvar and Solvar through their sound changes, grammar and parallel passages.

title: Identity, sounds and word formation
description: The names of the dwarven peoples and their languages, followed by Korvar pronunciation and the rules for forming words.

title: The common grammar
description: Korvar noun cases, verbs and sentence patterns, with worked examples for questions, possession, conditions and measurement.

title: Stone and material vocabulary
description: Korvar words distinguish a rock’s appearance from its composition and tested uses. The vocabulary also covers machinery, soil and household care.

title: Writing, numbers and everyday use
description: Learn the Stavmark script, decimal counting and everyday forms of address. Reading passages and exercises put them into use.

title: Practitioners and magical work
description: How practitioners learn their work and use it for healing, protection, communication and travel, within the laws and customs of their communities.

title: Magic in everyday life
description: People seek magic for wounds, wards, journeys and local hazards. Its usefulness depends on training, preparation and access to a practitioner.

title: Reading public atlas descriptions
description: How to read the atlas’s geographic notes and distinguish terrain, habitats and historical movement. Map illustrations are awaiting revision.

title: Merenval: landscapes, travel and communities
description: Merenval’s coasts, the companion’s plateaus and caverns, rare interworld journeys and life within Dorrenath.

title: Merenval and its living companion
description: Merenval and its inhabited companion share long days and slow tides. Their seas, forests and cavern lands are home to Elves, Gnomes and Orcs.

title: Orcs
description: Orc communities span both worlds, from cities and farms to mobile bands. Their customs address strength, agreed challenges and obligations to others.

title: The Otherworld in human stories and reports
description: Human travelers tell of strange roads, fay hospitality and journeys with uncertain endings. Their accounts often disagree about what they encountered.

title: Public persons, beliefs, and dangerous boundaries
description: Amadeus Cordelien’s religious office and promises, differing creation beliefs, and fragmentary warnings about the Howling Void.

title: The worlds and their skies
description: Each main world has its own sun. Their inhabitants navigate and keep time under very different conditions of light.

title: The Thals
description: Thal refugees reached Dverghamar about 40,000 years ago, changed by a flight that carried people, animals and plants from Erde.

title: Dverghamar: habitats and wildlife
description: Dverghamar’s wildlife occupies moist slopes, lakes, caves and scattered refuges. Many species remain undescribed.
